title: Credit deconflict: delta-claim protocol for provisional usage and safe commit
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: At-least-once ingest patterns combined with client retries and network flakiness create duplicate charge risk. Existing ledger and reservation systems either over-reserve (blocking capacity) or under-protect (leading to duplicate charges after retries). Goal: implement a server-driven 'delta-claim' flow where clients obtain provisional delta credits for an in-flight request and later commit a deterministic delta that is idempotent across retries. The protocol must integrate with rate limiting, per-customer quotas, and streaming/chunked generation, and must be compatible with hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Server issues a short-lived provisional delta id when a request would consume billable tokens; provisional delta is visible in per-customer pending reservations dashboard
Clients can return a commit containing (delta_id, deterministic_nonce, token_count) and server applies delta exactly-once despite retries
If client fails to commit within the provisional TTL, the provisional delta expires and is reconciled without double-charging
Protocol enforces per-route and per-customer concurrency limits and responds deterministically under contention
End-to-end test coverage simulating network retries and client crashes shows no duplicate final charges across 1000 randomized scenarios
Metrics: pending_reservations, provisional_expirations, duplicate_commit_rejects <= 0 for baseline tests, reconciliation_corrections tracked and audited
steps: Design delta_claim API shape (POST /v1/usage/provisional -> returns delta_id, expires_at, lease_seq)
Implement provisional reservation store with TTL, tied to customer_id + route + model_variant
Add commit endpoint (POST /v1/usage/commit) that accepts delta_id, client_nonce, final_tokens, client_signature (optional for Private)
Ensure commit path is idempotent: commit is accepted only once per (delta_id, client_nonce) pair and additional identical commits are no-ops
Wire provisional reservation metrics to Console and billing pipeline; add reconciliation sweep job that converts expired provisional deltas to no-charge or refunded reservations depending on policy
Integrate with runtime rate limiter: provisional reservations decrement available quota, but can be preempted by higher-priority allocations under configured policies
Write deterministic model for streaming/chunked responses: per-chunk provisional deltas and a final commit that rolls up chunks
Add SDK helpers (node/python) to manage provisional->commit lifecycle with exponential backoff on commit failures
Create end-to-end test harness and chaos scenarios; run staging releases on Dedicated and Private environments
implementation_notes: Reservation storage: implement as strongly-consistent KV entries (etcd or coordinator DB) keyed by customer:delta_id to prevent split-brain in Dedicated/Private
Lease sequencing: include monotonic lease_seq from server to detect stale client commits; server rejects commit if server-side lease_seq advanced beyond delta's recorded sequence
Conflict resolution: if two clients attempt to claim same logical work, first provisional wins; second receives preempt_code and a deterministic retry window to obtain new delta
Fallback policy: if commit path is unreachable for >TTL, reconciliation marks provisional as expired and flags request for manual review if usage > threshold
Cost visibility: provisional reservations count toward 'reserved' quota in console to prevent overcommit; this may increase apparent used quota briefly
Security: require signed client_nonce for Private deployments integrated with KMS; hosted may use HMAC secret per-project
Performance: keep provisional path cheap (single KV write). Commit should be optimized sync-path to ledger with batched commit frames to reduce IO under high QPS
Edge cases: long-lived streaming requests should renew provisional TTL periodically; aborted streams must send explicit abort with delta_id to expedite reconciliation
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Decided on server-issued delta_id + client_nonce idempotency model instead of client-generated UUIDs to avoid clock drift issues (vote: 6-1)
2026-03-11: Chose strong consistency for provisional store in Dedicated/Private to avoid split-brain billing; hosted will use leader-coordinated cluster (note: minor performance cost accepted)

2026-03-12: Opted for 'no-charge on expiration' as default reconciliation policy with an opt-in 'automatic finalization' for enterprise customers that prefer optimistic reservations (to lower reconciliation noise)
2026-03-12: Require security review for KMS integration and signed commits (owner: security team)

2026-03-12 - Security Team: security_review_required=true. We'll schedule an architecture review for 2026-03-18. Private deployment requires client signature validation using customer KMS

test_plan: Unit tests for provisional store invariants (single-writer semantics)
Integration tests: client obtains provisional, sends duplicate commits; server should accept one and ignore rest
Chaos tests: simulate server restart during commit and ensure commit persists exactly once
Scale tests: 50k provisional/sec sustained for 10m in staging to measure KV write amplification
Billing reconciliation simulation: run against historical production traces and validate zero net-double-charges on 30-day window
rollout_and_migration: Phase 0 (canary): enable delta_claim on runtime-1.26 for 5% of hosted traffic; monitor pending_reservations and provisional_expirations
Phase 1 (staging): enable SDK helpers and run full chaos suite on Dedicated cluster
Phase 2 (gradual): opt-in customers for automatic finalization; default behavior remains no-charge on expiration
Migration notes: legacy tokens without delta support will continue to be billed via existing ledger; we'll provide a reconciliation tool to map old events to new commitments
Rollback criteria: >0.1% reconciliation_corrections or increase in customer support refunds > baseline for 24h
